A combine that decides its own path

01 · Algorithm

What the demo cannot explain on its own

The projector shows the result: the machines move and the wheat disappears. These four decisions are what make that movement efficient rather than a random walk.

Furrow path

The field is split into parallel lanes exactly as wide as the header. The machine runs one lane end to end, turns 180 degrees at the headland and enters the next one in the opposite direction. It is the same pattern a plough follows: back and forth, without lifting the cut.

Sequential vs. alternating lanes

Entering the immediately adjacent lane would demand a tighter turn than the machine's real turning radius allows. So the route skips a lane and comes back later for the ones it left: every turn gets the space the combine physically needs.

Headland trim

Before laying out the lanes, the algorithm reserves a perimeter strip as wide as the turning radius. The lanes only occupy the inner rectangle, and the headland stays clear for manoeuvring without leaving the field.

Spatial grid

The field is subdivided into cells and every stalk is registered in its own. Instead of checking more than a thousand stalks per frame to know which ones the header cuts, only the cells the header touches at that instant are queried.

02 · Architecture

From the configuration panel to the field

The configuration is defined before entering the simulation and travels between scenes. Once inside, the combine is the only one that decides the route; the tractor reacts to it.

  1. Configuration panel

    The user defines the field and the machines before starting.

    ▼

  2. ConfiguracionSimulacion

    Preserves those values across the scene change.

    ▼

  3. Simulation scene

    Generates the terrain, the stalks and the agents.

    ▼

  4. Combine harvester (leader)

    Computes the furrow route and performs the cut.

    ▼

  5. Tractor (follower)

    Holds its lateral position relative to the leader.

Project scripts

  • Cosechadora.cs

    Lays out the lanes, executes the headland turns and cuts the stalks under the header.

  • TractorAlLado.cs

    Keeps the tractor and its trailer alongside the combine as it advances.

  • ParcelaSpawner.cs

    Procedurally generates the terrain, the stalks and the environment props.

  • PanelConfiguracionUI.cs

    Builds the interface where the parameters are set before simulating.

  • ConfiguracionSimulacion.cs

    Data bridge that survives the scene change and carries the configuration.

  • SelectorModelo.cs

    Lets you choose which 3D model is instantiated per machine.

  • CameraMove.cs

    Drives the four observation cameras and the switching between them.

05 · Roadmap

What shipped and what comes next

Shipped

  1. ✓

    Procedural route

    Lanes and turns computed from the field dimensions.

  2. ✓

    Cutting optimised with a spatial grid

    Neighbour cell lookups instead of walking every stalk.

  3. ✓

    Companion tractor

    Lateral following of the combine with the trailer hitched.

  4. ✓

    Procedural terrain population

    Stalks, trees and environment generated on every run.

  5. ✓

    Configuration panel

    Parameters adjustable before the simulation starts.

  6. ✓

    Four cameras

    Switchable views to observe the system from several angles.

Next

  1. →

    Tractor as a real autonomous agent

    Its own decisions instead of rigid following of the leader.

  2. →

    Instantiate N machines from configuration

    A fleet of variable size coordinating over the same field.

  3. →

    Obstacle avoidance with NavMesh

    Routes that dodge environment and other machines without stopping.

  4. →

    Efficiency metrics per machine

    Distance, overlap and idle time measured per agent.

Why it matters

Every one of these pieces points at the same place: precision agriculture. A well planned route burns less fuel, a lane pattern without overlap avoids harvesting the same strip twice, and a fleet that coordinates on its own cuts the idle time between passes. What is a university simulation here is, out in the field, measurable operating margin.
